threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Dalston Junction is a fancy place, but the locals just call it 'that station with all the pigeons.'
Caught a couple arguing about Jollof rice on the 59 last night. Turns out, he prefers rice from a spot in Peckham. The passion was real.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home once I spotted the old Turkish guy selling fresh gözleme from his cart at Sonnenallee every Sunday morning. The line tells you everything.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop where the butcher also serves craft beer. It’s the kind of quirky mix that makes late nights here feel uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re a local when you can tell how bad the BART delays are just by the number of people lined up at the taco truck.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus the other day, five people got on with burritos. They just kept passing around a hot sauce bottle. Classic Mission vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the locals love the plaça, but most of us avoid it. Too noisy, too many selfies. We prefer our corner bars away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still carry a plastic map—locals just rely on their phones and the occasional paella recommendation.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the tube' when you mean the Overground, and you haven't realized Hackney is a whole vibe, not just a postcode.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old Spice Girls hits. Even the driver was chuckling. Brixton nights, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a toddler in a pink tutu riding a bicycle with a parrot on her shoulder near Reuterplatz. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a taco stand next to a classic currywurst joint, where lunchtime debates merge flavors and cultures seamlessly.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they expertly dodge those potholes on Valencia while juggling a burrito and a coffee. Tourists just step in them.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 38 Geary playing a ukulele while the bus jerked to a stop. Every strum matched the bumps, like he was composing a song just for us.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is only about Gaudí, but the real gems are the tiny plazas where locals sip café amb llet, not the famous park.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always stand staring at the metro map, not realizing Google Maps is often more confusing underground than above.
